chapter: Chicago pioneers, community and New Orleans brotherhood
title: Charles Elgar and the Navy Pier Ballroom
summary: Saunders remembers Elgar's band at the Navy Pier ballroom and discusses plans to restore it and hold a jazz festival there.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Right. Well, see, all of those guys were very, very -- and another good friend of mine from New Orleans, who had a band here years ago, I never had the pleasure of working with him, Mr. Elgar. I always called -- Charles Elgar. And his band -- man, I mean, he wore tails, and big, tall, six-two or something like that, thin, and he looked like a prince. Real, real -- and he worked at Paddy Harmon's Dreamland for years. He worked at the old -- this brings back memories to me -- the old Navy Pier Ballroom there. This was a big ballroom there on -- out on the lake.
At the end of the pier?
Right, and see, they're trying to rejuvenate it now.
Yeah, I did a couple of things down there last year.
Yeah, and I just read in the paper a couple of days ago --
(Inaudible.)
Oh, beautiful out there, oh, yeah. Big dome and the lights all in there.
(Inaudible) all refurbished.
Right, right. Well, what they're talking about now is the fountain system and the accoustics. They're going to spend I don't know how much money to try to rejuvenate the sound.
Yeah, it's a little echo-y.
Right.
It's a little hard to hear on the stage.
Well, yeah, so the city is spending quite a bit of money now.
I know they're very interested in the Navy Pier.
Right.
Bill Snyder -- you know Bill?
Yeah.
I talked to him today. He wants to do a jazz festival out on the pier in September, and get the city behind it.
Right, right, right.
Have bands and groups strung out all across the whole pier.
That's a beautiful place. 2,000 -- I think it'll seat about 2,000 people.
Yeah.
But that used to be the ballroom, and they had Charles Elgar with his great band there. They used to play, and they used to broadcast.
What a great place to --
Oh, man, that's wonderful. It's beautiful there, right, right, right.
Plus they've got permanent seating in it now.
Oh, I haven't been in since they rejuvenated it.
Yeah, they have, like, theatre seating in it. I think. Maybe -- it might be chairs, I think maybe, come to think of it, it is. It can be cleared.
I would imagine they would do that, because for different type of events. They would not put anything stationary in there.
I wish they would.
